title: Mickanic — Real-Time Bidding & Service Marketplace Platform
description: I architected a service-based marketplace using Next.js 16 and Bun, integrating real-time bidding, Socket.io messaging, and tiered Stripe subscriptions, backed by PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ.

contextBlocks.label: The Problem
contextBlocks.body: Drivers needed a platform to post vehicle-service jobs, while mechanics needed a centralized place to browse jobs, submit bids, and manage subscriptions. A seamless way to connect and communicate was required for the Mickanic platform.

contextBlocks.label: The Solution
contextBlocks.body: I developed a service-based marketplace connecting consumers and contractors. The solution features a Next.js frontend and a Bun-powered API, featuring real-time Socket.io messaging and RabbitMQ background workers.

architectureLayers.name: Client / UI
architectureLayers.description: Frontend application catering to Admin, Consumer, and Contractor roles.

architectureLayers.name: API & Compute
architectureLayers.description: High-performance backend API and WebSocket server.

architectureLayers.name: Data Layer
architectureLayers.description: Relational database, caching, and object storage.

architectureLayers.name: Infra / Delivery
architectureLayers.description: Containerized orchestration and asynchronous task queues.

features.title: Real-Time Bidding & Messaging
features.description: Implemented a real-time messaging system between consumers and contractors using Socket.IO. The frontend utilizes Redux Toolkit Query alongside real-time hooks to manage conversations and typing indicators without full page reloads.
highlights: Instant bid updates & chat sync across active browser clients
Optimistic state updates via Redux Toolkit Query handlers
Typing indicators & read receipt state management

features.title: Tiered Subscription Engine
features.description: Integrated tiered subscription plans (Basic, Premium, Pro) for contractors, which govern job application limits, lead costs, and platform visibility. Stripe is used for handling the subscription and payment workflows.
highlights: Dynamic job bidding quota management based on tier levels
Stripe Customer Portal integration for effortless plan upgrades
Idempotent webhook handlers for subscription lifecycle events

features.title: Event-Driven Background Processing
features.description: Offloaded heavy processing like email delivery and web-push notifications to a background worker using RabbitMQ. This ensures the main API remains responsive during high-traffic events, with an hourly email limit of 150 strictly enforced.
features.media:
email-worker:
  image: sandraluty-backend
  command: bun run email_worker:prod
  depends_on:

highlights: Isolated background containerized execution via Docker Compose
Bun runtime execution for fast startup & minimal memory overhead
Rate-limited queue consumer processing strictly 150 emails/hour

metrics.label: Hourly email sending limit via RabbitMQ
Type safety with Prisma and TypeScript

entries.heading: Real-Time State Synchronization
entries.detail: Keeping the optimistic UI in sync with backend state was complex. We leveraged Redux Toolkit Query to cache data and refresh active conversations automatically upon receiving Socket.IO events.

entries.heading: Asynchronous Notification Delivery
entries.detail: Blocking the main thread for transactional emails degraded performance. Implementing RabbitMQ allowed us to queue tasks like contact_auto_reply, handling them via a dedicated Bun email worker.

entries.heading: Infrastructure Orchestration
entries.detail: Bundling PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ within a single docker-compose.yml file simplified local development and ensured parity across environments.

entries.heading: Schema-Driven Type Safety
entries.detail: Using Prisma allowed us to define a single schema for users, contractors, jobs, and bids. Generating the client directly from the schema ensured reliable database operations.
